claims.claim: Experienced open-source developers were 19% slower with AI while believing they were 20% faster, having forecast 24% faster beforehand
claims.sample: 16 developers, 246 real tasks in repositories they knew deeply, randomized per task
claims.cautions: Authors' own scope caveat: deeply-understood repos are close to a worst case for these tools. METR published a design update in February 2026 — treat the figure as of its date.

claims.claim: AI raised productivity by about 0.29% on average over three years, with 89% of firms reporting no impact at all; firms forecast 1.4% over the next three
claims.source: Yotzov, Barrero, Bloom, Bunn, Davis, Foster et al.
claims.sample: stratified survey of 5,000+ CFOs, CEOs and executives across the US, UK, Germany and Australia
claims.cautions: The mean is a near-zero mass with a concentrated tail, NOT a small uniform gain. Do not paraphrase as 'modest gains'.

claims.claim: Precise null effects on earnings and hours, ruling out effects larger than 2%; users self-report 2.8% time savings against RCT gains exceeding 15% in the same occupations
claims.sample: Danish worker- and workplace-level administrative data
claims.cautions: Paper has been revised and retitled — cite the current version.
